quests.conceptTitle: Simple Present: Habitual Actions
quests.faultySentence: These days, she usually cooked dinner for her family after work.
quests.correctedSentence: These days, she usually cooks dinner for her family after work.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'These days' signals a present habit, so the verb should be in the simple present, 'cooks', not the past tense 'cooked'.
quests.nativeTip: 'These days' points to a current habit — what tense expresses repeated actions happening now?

quests.conceptTitle: Simple Past: Past Habitual Actions
quests.faultySentence: Last summer, we usually go to the beach on weekends.
quests.correctedSentence: Last summer, we usually went to the beach on weekends.
quests.ruleExplanation: Because 'last summer' describes a completed period, the habitual action needs the simple past 'went', not the present form 'go'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Last summer' refers to a finished time period — what tense fits repeated past actions?

quests.conceptTitle: Simple Present: General Facts and Schedules
quests.faultySentence: The store opened at nine every morning, according to the sign.
quests.correctedSentence: The store opens at nine every morning, according to the sign.
quests.ruleExplanation: General facts and standing schedules use the simple present, so 'opens' is correct instead of the past tense 'opened'.
quests.nativeTip: This sentence states a standing rule about store hours — what tense do general facts use?

quests.conceptTitle: Simple Future: Will for Predictions
quests.faultySentence: I think it rain tomorrow.
quests.correctedSentence: I think it will rain tomorrow.
quests.ruleExplanation: A prediction about tomorrow needs the future form 'will rain', not the base verb 'rain'.
quests.nativeTip: The word 'tomorrow' points to the future, and 'I think' signals a prediction — what future form fits?

quests.conceptTitle: Future with Going To: Correct Formation
quests.faultySentence: She is go to start a new job next Monday.
quests.correctedSentence: She is going to start a new job next Monday.
quests.ruleExplanation: The 'going to' future requires 'be' plus 'going', so the sentence needs 'is going', not 'is go'.
quests.nativeTip: The 'going to' future needs a form of 'be' plus the -ing form of 'go' — what's missing here?

quests.conceptTitle: Simple Future: Will + Base Verb
quests.faultySentence: The flight will leaving at seven tomorrow morning.
quests.correctedSentence: The flight will leave at seven tomorrow morning.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Will' is always followed by the base form of the verb, so the sentence needs 'will leave', not 'will leaving'.
quests.nativeTip: After 'will', the main verb should be in its base form — check the verb ending here.

quests.conceptTitle: Simple Past: Irregular Verb Formation
quests.faultySentence: Yesterday, I seen my old classmate at the mall.
quests.correctedSentence: Yesterday, I saw my old classmate at the mall.
quests.ruleExplanation: Without an auxiliary like 'have', the simple past of 'see' is 'saw', not the participle form 'seen'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Seen' is a past participle — what is the simple past form of 'see' used without a helping verb?

quests.conceptTitle: Simple Past: Irregular Verb Formation
quests.faultySentence: He come to the office late three times last week.
quests.correctedSentence: He came to the office late three times last week.
quests.ruleExplanation: The simple past of 'come' is the irregular form 'came'; 'come' alone is the base form, which doesn't show past tense here.
quests.nativeTip: Without a helping verb, choose the simple past form of 'come', not the base form.

quests.conceptTitle: Simple Past: Irregular Verb Formation
quests.faultySentence: We eaten breakfast before the meeting started.
quests.correctedSentence: We ate breakfast before the meeting started.
quests.ruleExplanation: Without an auxiliary verb, the sentence needs the simple past 'ate' rather than the past participle 'eaten'.
quests.nativeTip: There's no helping verb like 'had' here — what simple past form of 'eat' is needed?

quests.conceptTitle: Verb Tense Consistency in a Sentence
quests.faultySentence: She opened the door and sees a huge surprise waiting for her.
quests.correctedSentence: She opened the door and saw a huge surprise waiting for her.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'opened' is in the simple past, the second action should match: 'saw', not the present-tense 'sees'.
quests.nativeTip: Both actions happen at the same time in the past — should the second verb also be in the past tense?

quests.conceptTitle: Verb Tense Consistency in a Sentence
quests.faultySentence: Every morning, he wakes up early and made his bed before breakfast.
quests.correctedSentence: Every morning, he wakes up early and makes his bed before breakfast.
quests.ruleExplanation: Because the sentence describes a routine ('every morning'), both actions should be in the present tense: 'wakes' and 'makes', not the past 'made'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Every morning' signals a repeated present habit — should both verbs stay in the present tense?

quests.conceptTitle: Verb Tense Consistency in a Sentence
quests.faultySentence: The technician arrived on time and fixes the printer within an hour.
quests.correctedSentence: The technician arrived on time and fixed the printer within an hour.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'arrived' places the sentence in the past, the second verb must also be past tense: 'fixed', not the present 'fixes'.
quests.nativeTip: The first verb, 'arrived', sets the time frame — should the second verb match that same past time?

quests.conceptTitle: Simple Past Negative: Did Not + Base Verb
quests.faultySentence: I didn't went to the party last night.
quests.correctedSentence: I didn't go to the party last night.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Didn't' already carries the past tense, so the verb after it must be the base form 'go', not the past form 'went'.
quests.nativeTip: After 'didn't', the main verb should return to its base form — check the verb here.

quests.conceptTitle: Simple Past Questions: Did + Base Verb
quests.faultySentence: Did you went to the bank yesterday?
quests.correctedSentence: Did you go to the bank yesterday?
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'did' already shows the past tense, the main verb after it must stay in the base form: 'go', not 'went'.
quests.nativeTip: Questions with 'did' need the base form of the verb — is 'went' the base form?

quests.conceptTitle: Negative Verb Forms: Be vs Do in Past Tense
quests.faultySentence: He wasn't finish the assignment before the deadline.
quests.correctedSentence: He didn't finish the assignment before the deadline.
quests.ruleExplanation: Action verbs form the past negative with 'didn't', not a form of 'be' like 'wasn't', so the sentence needs 'didn't finish'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Finish' is an action verb — should its past negative use a form of 'be' or a form of 'do'?

quests.conceptTitle: Future Time Clauses: Present in the Clause, Future in the Main Sentence
quests.faultySentence: When she arrives at the airport, she called her sister.
quests.correctedSentence: When she arrives at the airport, she will call her sister.
quests.ruleExplanation: In sentences about future time, the time clause uses the present tense ('arrives'), while the main clause uses the future: 'will call'.
quests.nativeTip: 'When she arrives' describes a future event using the present tense — what tense should the main clause use?

quests.conceptTitle: Future Time Clauses: Present Tense After Before/After/When
quests.faultySentence: Before the movie will start tonight, we are going to grab some snacks.
quests.correctedSentence: Before the movie starts tonight, we are going to grab some snacks.
quests.ruleExplanation: Even though the sentence refers to the future, the clause after 'before' uses the simple present 'starts', not 'will start'.
quests.nativeTip: Time clauses beginning with 'before' describing future events use the present tense, not 'will'.

quests.conceptTitle: Future Time Clauses: Present Tense After Before/After/When
quests.faultySentence: After the manager will approve the budget, the team can start the project.
quests.correctedSentence: After the manager approves the budget, the team can start the project.
quests.ruleExplanation: Clauses introduced by 'after' that refer to future events use the simple present, so 'approves' is correct instead of 'will approve'.
quests.nativeTip: The clause starting with 'after' refers to a future event — should it use 'will' or the simple present?

quests.conceptTitle: Future Negative: Be Able To + Infinitive
quests.faultySentence: I won't be able attend the meeting tomorrow.
quests.correctedSentence: I won't be able to attend the meeting tomorrow.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Be able' must be followed by 'to' plus the base verb, so the sentence needs 'be able to attend'.
quests.nativeTip: The phrase 'be able' needs a small connecting word before the next verb — what's missing?

quests.conceptTitle: Present Perfect Negative: Have Not + Past Participle
quests.faultySentence: They haven't decide yet where to go for vacation.
quests.correctedSentence: They haven't decided yet where to go for vacation.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Haven't' requires the past participle, so the sentence needs 'decided', not the base form 'decide'.
quests.nativeTip: After 'haven't', the verb should take its past participle form — what is that form of 'decide'?

quests.conceptTitle: Simple Past Negative: Did Not + Base Verb
quests.faultySentence: She didn't finished her degree because she moved abroad.
quests.correctedSentence: She didn't finish her degree because she moved abroad.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Didn't' already marks the past tense, so 'finish' should stay in its base form rather than 'finished'.
quests.nativeTip: After 'didn't', the main verb returns to its base form — check the ending here.

quests.conceptTitle: Simple Past Questions: Did + Subject + Base Verb
quests.faultySentence: Where does she went last weekend?
quests.correctedSentence: Where did she go last weekend?
quests.ruleExplanation: Past-time questions use 'did' with the base form of the verb, so the sentence needs 'did she go', not 'does she went'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Last weekend' shows this is a past-time question — which auxiliary and verb form fit together?

quests.conceptTitle: Subject-Verb Agreement in Questions
quests.faultySentence: How many people is coming to the party?
quests.correctedSentence: How many people are coming to the party?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'People' is plural, so the present continuous question needs 'are coming', not the singular 'is coming'.
quests.nativeTip: 'How many people' asks about a plural group — what form of 'be' matches a plural subject?

quests.conceptTitle: Future Questions: Will + Base Verb
quests.faultySentence: What time will the store closes tonight?
quests.correctedSentence: What time will the store close tonight?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Will' is always followed by the base verb, so the question needs 'will close', not 'will closes'.
quests.nativeTip: After 'will' in a question, the verb should stay in its base form — check the ending.

quests.conceptTitle: Future with Going To: Correct Formation
quests.faultySentence: Look at those clouds — it going to rain soon.
quests.correctedSentence: Look at those clouds — it's going to rain soon.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Going to' requires a form of 'be', so the sentence needs 'it's going' (it is going), not 'it going'.
quests.nativeTip: The 'going to' future always needs a form of 'be' before 'going' — what's missing here?

quests.conceptTitle: Simple Future: Will + Base Verb
quests.faultySentence: By next year, she will graduating from college.
quests.correctedSentence: By next year, she will graduate from college.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Will' must be followed by the base verb, so the sentence needs 'will graduate', not the -ing form 'graduating'.
quests.nativeTip: After 'will', use the base form of the verb — is 'graduating' the base form?

quests.conceptTitle: Simple Future: Will + Base Verb
quests.faultySentence: The new policy will affects everyone in the department.
quests.correctedSentence: The new policy will affect everyone in the department.
quests.ruleExplanation: Verbs after 'will' never take an -s ending, so the sentence needs 'will affect', not 'will affects'.
quests.nativeTip: Check the verb right after 'will' — should it carry an -s ending?

quests.conceptTitle: Simple Present: Recurring Actions
quests.faultySentence: Every Friday, the department submit its weekly reports.
quests.correctedSentence: Every Friday, the department submits its weekly reports.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The department' is singular, and 'every Friday' shows a routine, so the present tense needs 'submits'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Every Friday' signals a repeated action — what verb ending matches a singular subject like 'the department'?

quests.conceptTitle: Simple Past: Completed Actions
quests.faultySentence: Last year, the company launch three new products.
quests.correctedSentence: Last year, the company launched three new products.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Last year' indicates the action is already complete, so the verb needs the past-tense ending: 'launched'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Last year' places this action in a finished period — what past-tense ending fits?

quests.conceptTitle: Simple Future: Will + Base Verb
quests.faultySentence: Next month, the clinic will opens a new branch downtown.
quests.correctedSentence: Next month, the clinic will open a new branch downtown.
quests.ruleExplanation: The future tense 'will' always takes the base verb, so the sentence needs 'will open', not 'will opens'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Next month' points to the future — check the verb form right after 'will'.
